title: Splicedock
description: A single MCP gateway for tools, profiles, policies, and Code Mode.
text: Connect your agents to one gateway and manage which tools each agent can use. One path to your tools Agents connect over MCP. Splicedock routes calls to MCP servers, HTTP APIs, and CLI tools. Get started Run a local example Connect an MCP client Configure access profiles Run a Code Mode workflow Version 1.0 This guide describes Splicedock 1.0 and its MCP, HTTP, and CLI integrations. Where policy applies Gateway policies apply to calls routed through Splicedock. Local files, a client shell, and permissions within backend services need their own controls.

title: Quickstart
description: Start Splicedock locally, authenticate, and verify your first tool result.
text: This example exposes the installed Node.js version. It needs no external backend. 1. Prepare the environment Install Git, Node.js 22, and npm. Install dependencies under the same Node version that runs the gateway so the native SQLite module is compatible. Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] git clone https://github.com/kamilrybacki/cellarette.git splicedock cd splicedock npm ci npm run build Copy 2. Save the configuration Copy the demo configuration from the checkout. The demo profile exposes demo__version and enables Code Mode. The example disables strong consent for this read-only demo. Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] cp site/examples/quickstart.yaml splicedock.local.yaml Copy View the example configuration Example configuration [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] # Local, read-only demo. Strong WebAuthn consent is disabled for this demo only. server: port: 8788 admin_port: 8789 admin_token_env: SPLICEDOCK_ADMIN_TOKEN require_profile_token: true cli_whitelist: [node] consent: enabled: false profiles: default: tools: ["__no_tools__"] demo: tools: ["demo__version"] enable_code_mode: true tools: - type: cli name: version namespace: demo description: "Read the installed Node.js version" command: node args: ["--version"] Copy 3. Start the application Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] export SPLICEDOCK_CONFIG="$PWD/splicedock.local.yaml" export SPLICEDOCK_DB_PATH="$PWD/.data/splicedock.db" export SPLICEDOCK_ADMIN_TOKEN="$(node -e 'console.log(require("node:crypto").randomBytes(32).toString("hex"))')" node dist/index.js & gateway_pid=$! Copy Run the next command in the same terminal so it can use the administrator token. The gateway serves MCP on port 8788 and the Admin API on 8789 . For this example use a local machine with those ports available. 4. Make your first tool call The example issues a short-lived profile token, lists tools, and calls demo__version over MCP. Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] node site/examples/first-call.mjs Copy Example output [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] demo__version: v22.14.0 Copy The version should match node --version in the same terminal. The example revokes its token when it finishes. To connect your own client, create a separate profile token . 5. Stop the demo To stop the local gateway, run the following command in the terminal where it started. Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] kill "$gateway_pid" Copy

title: MCP clients and tokens
description: Create, rotate, and revoke a token for an MCP client.
text: Use an MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP and an Authorization header. Two kinds of token Token Purpose Administrator Manage profiles, tokens, and approvals. Profile Authenticate an MCP client and select its permitted tools. Create a profile token The Quickstart creates the demo profile. To connect with a different profile, replace its name in the request. Run the following with your administrator token. Admin API [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] curl --fail-with-body -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8789/api/v1/profile-tokens \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SPLICEDOCK_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"profile":"demo","agent":"my-agent","expires_in_seconds":3600}' Copy HTTP 201 returns data.token and data.id . Save the raw token in your client’s secret store when it is issued. Configure the client Connection settings [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] transport: Streamable HTTP url: http://127.0.0.1:8788/mcp header: Authorization: Bearer <PROFILE_TOKEN> Copy The exact configuration field names depend on your client. Reconnect after changing them. How the profile is selected The bearer token selects its bound profile. Connect to /mcp with Authorization: Bearer <PROFILE_TOKEN> . With server.require_profile_token: true , a missing, unknown, expired, or revoked token returns HTTP 401. Rotate or revoke a token Action Endpoint List tokens GET /api/v1/profile-tokens Rotate POST /api/v1/profile-tokens/:id/rotate Revoke POST /api/v1/profile-tokens/:id/revoke with reason manual or compromised Rotation returns HTTP 201. Save the new data.token in your client’s secret store and reconnect. Keep data.id for the next rotation or revocation. Send {"reason":"manual"} to revoke a token. HTTP 204 confirms revocation. Admin UI mutations using a session cookie require X-Splicedock-CSRF .

title: Profiles and YAML
description: Configure the tool catalog, Code Mode, and credential bindings.
text: A profile limits the names a client can discover and call. Tool policies still apply to individual calls. Profile manifest Existing profile [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - "demo__version" enable_code_mode: true credentials: {} Copy Use exact tool names or globs. A new manifest includes name . Code Mode has an explicit flag and is disabled by default. Edit in the browser Open /admin/profiles , select a profile, edit the YAML, and save. The editor validates the document and retains its comments. Revisions and conflicts Saves include base_revision . If somebody else has saved since you opened the editor, HTTP 409 asks you to reload and reconcile the changes. Storage and restart YAML configuration seeds missing profiles at startup. The catalog keeps committed manifests in the database. A deleted configuration profile stays deleted across restarts. Manifest API List profiles with GET /api/v1/profiles . Request the YAML catalog with ?format=yaml . Use the profile editor for revision-aware updates.

title: Backends and tools
description: Connect MCP, HTTP and CLI backends.
text: Choose a driver for the system you are integrating and add its exposed names to the appropriate profiles. Choose a driver Driver Use it for mcp_proxy Connect an existing MCP server. http Expose one operation from a web API. cli Run a predefined command with a fixed argument template. cli_passthrough Accept an argument array and apply a policy before running it. Start from the Quickstart configuration . Merge the shown keys into the existing YAML, keeping other tools and allowlist entries. Restart the gateway after editing it. If the profile already exists, update its tool list in the profile editor . Connect with a token for that profile , then call the named tool in your MCP client. The JSON snippets show the request sent by the client. Start the local MCP and HTTP demo server From the repository checkout, after installing dependencies, run this command in a separate terminal. The demo server source binds to 127.0.0.1:9001 . Start it before the gateway on the same machine. Stop it with Ctrl+C. Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] node site/examples/driver-backends.mjs Copy mcp_proxy http cli cli_passthrough MCP server The local demo server exposes lookup_product . Splicedock adds the backend name as a prefix, so the client calls catalog__lookup_product . Gateway configuration [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - type: mcp_proxy name: catalog service_dns: 127.0.0.1 port: 9001 transport: streamable_http Copy Add this tool to the profile manifest [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - catalog__lookup_product Copy MCP tools/call request [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "catalog__lookup_product", "arguments": { "sku": "P-100" } } } Copy Example result text [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] P-100: Desk lamp Copy Use the hostname as seen from the gateway. The configured host and port form an HTTP URL ending in /mcp for Streamable HTTP or /sse for SSE. HTTP endpoint Look up a product in the demo API by SKU. The gateway URL-encodes the sku argument and puts it in the path. Gateway configuration [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - type: http namespace: catalog name: product description: Look up a product by SKU method: GET url: http://127.0.0.1:9001/products/{sku} params: - name: sku in: path required: true auth: { type: none } Copy Add this tool to the profile manifest [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - catalog__product Copy MCP tools/call request [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "catalog__product", "arguments": { "sku": "P-100" } } } Copy Example result text [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] {"sku":"P-100","name":"Desk lamp"} Copy Authenticate to an HTTP backend For a backend that requires a bearer token, replace the tool’s auth block with the following and set CATALOG_API_TOKEN in the gateway environment. Point url at that API, using HTTPS for a remote backend. HTTP tool authentication [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] auth: type: bearer token: from: env:CATALOG_API_TOKEN Copy Fixed CLI command Expose node --version as a tool with no arguments. Node.js must be on the gateway’s PATH . If you are using the Quickstart configuration, keep its existing entry for this tool. Gateway configuration [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] server: cli_whitelist: [node] tools: - type: cli namespace: demo name: version description: Read the installed Node.js version command: node args: ["--version"] Copy Add this tool to the profile manifest [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - demo__version Copy MCP tools/call request [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "demo__version", "arguments": {} } } Copy Example result text [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] v22.14.0 Copy Compare the result with node --version in the gateway environment. CLI passthrough Expose Git and allow exactly one argument, version . Run command -v git in the gateway environment and use the resulting executable path in both YAML fields. Gateway configuration [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] server: cli_whitelist: [/usr/bin/git] tools: - type: cli_passthrough name: git description: Show the installed Git version command: /usr/bin/git policy: allow_subcommands: [version] max_args: 1 Copy Add this tool to the profile manifest [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - git__run Copy MCP tools/call request [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "git__run", "arguments": { "args": [ "version" ] } } } Copy Example result text [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] git version 2.43.0 Copy For a local setup, set a writable binary directory before starting the gateway. Terminal [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] export SPLICEDOCK_BIN="$PWD/.data/bin" Copy Check that the policy denies another command MCP tools/call request [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "git__run", "arguments": { "args": [ "status" ] } } } Copy Policy error text [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] Denied by policy.allow_subcommands Copy The gateway returns a tool error and does not start Git. See policy evaluation order for rule precedence.

title: Policies and approvals
description: Configure CLI rules and request approval for individual operations.
text: CLI passthrough checks the argument array before starting a process. Evaluation order The gateway checks the argument limit, deny rules, allow rules, and required arguments before handling approval. A hard denial takes precedence. Policy example kubectl tool policy [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] policy: max_args: 64 deny_subcommands: [delete] approval_subcommands: [apply] require_any_of: - ["--namespace", "-n"] audit: true Copy delete is denied. An apply request with a namespace flag requests approval. Request and consume approval The tool returns approval_id and expires_at . Wait through approvals__wait for up to 120 seconds per call. After approval, submit the same operation with the same token, profile, argument array, and resolved working directory before expiry. Each approval can be used once. Arguments for approvals__wait [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] {"id":"<APPROVAL_ID>","timeout_s":120} Copy Strong approval with WebAuthn Set server.consent.rp_id , its HTTPS origin , and the trusted hardware attestation roots. Configure the public origin used by the browser. Optional learned grants Enable SPLICEDOCK_GRANTS=1 to permit eligible operations after repeated successful approvals in similar contexts. Review or revoke grants in the admin panel.

title: Backend credentials
description: Use stored or short-lived credentials to reach a backend.
text: The agent uses a profile token. Splicedock selects the backend credential for the call. Credential selection Splicedock checks the profile binding, the deployment defaults, and the backend configuration in that order. Existing secret Profile fragment [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] credentials: gh: env: - name: GH_TOKEN from: env:GH_TOKEN_DEMO Copy Declare gh first and set the referenced variable on the gateway. Use an environment or Vault reference to keep the raw secret out of the YAML. Issue credentials on demand Define a provider in credential_providers and refer to it with mint in the profile. On first use the broker requests a credential, caches it, and refreshes it before expiry. Choose the backend credential’s minimum required scope. Profile binding [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] credentials: gh: env: - name: GH_TOKEN mint: github-app Copy The server must define the named github-app provider. It can run a configured helper that returns a GitHub App installation token.

title: Code Mode
description: Run several tool calls in one JavaScript workflow.
text: Give the gateway an async JavaScript function body. It runs the workflow and returns the result and a call summary. Enable the tool Profile manifest [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] tools: - "demo__version" enable_code_mode: true credentials: {} Copy The Quickstart enables Code Mode on demo . For another profile, set enable_code_mode: true , save, then refresh the client’s MCP catalog. Run a workflow Set the code argument on code_mode__execute . This example uses the quickstart . JavaScript [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] const response = await tools.call("demo__version", {}); return { ok: !response.isError, output: response.content }; Copy Discover and call tools API Returns tools.list() Names and descriptions. tools.search(query) Matching tools and schemas. await tools.call(name, args) An MCP tool result. Use Promise.all to run independent reads concurrently. Check isError and use the backend’s actual response shape. Sandbox and limits Resource Limit Input and final result 64 KiB each VM memory / stack 16 MiB / 512 KiB JS execution turn / workflow 1 s / 30 s Tool calls / concurrent calls 50 / 4 Tool response 4 MiB The QuickJS runtime has no direct filesystem, network, process, module loader, or timers. Code Mode cannot invoke itself. Simulate operations before execution To configure preflight, run a trusted local simulator and a separate reviewer, then select the profiles that should use them. Preflight prepares each HTTP request, MCP call, or CLI command and obtains a fixture from the simulator. The reviewer receives the snippet and trace. In enforcement mode, the gateway checks each live operation against the approved trace before sending or running it. Instance settings [ _ ] [ + ] [ x ] SPLICEDOCK_CODE_MODE_PREFLIGHT=observe SPLICEDOCK_CODE_MODE_PREFLIGHT_PROFILES=demo SPLICEDOCK_CODE_MODE_MOCK_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18953/mock SPLICEDOCK_CODE_MODE_REVIEW_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18953/review Copy Observe mode stops at review. Use enforce mode with a trusted review service that independently enforces operation permissions. A model score alone cannot authorize an operation. Use a profile token. HTTP, fixed CLI, CLI passthrough, and already connected Streamable HTTP MCP are supported. CLI passthrough applies its ordinary live policy and approvals. SSE is unsupported. Traffic produced inside a CLI process or remote MCP backend is outside this check. Errors, approvals, and retries Check each tool result and await all started operations. A later failure, timeout, or a changed preflight trace cannot roll back a call that has already started. A separate retry for an approved operation must obey the original policy.

title: Admin UI and observability
description: Use the admin panel, audit log, and Prometheus metrics.
text: The admin application normally listens on port 8789. Sign in with the administrator token. Sign in Open /admin/login on the admin origin. The browser uses a session cookie. API clients can send the administrator bearer token. Admin views View Use /admin/ Tool configuration and status. /admin/profiles Profile manifests. Audit Recent decisions. Approvals Pending operations and learned grants. Prometheus metrics Scrape /metrics on the admin port. Configure server.metrics_token_env for a separate metrics bearer token if required. Process counters can reset on restart. Phone notifications Configure the optional PWA and Web Push with SPLICEDOCK_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY , SPLICEDOCK_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY , and SPLICEDOCK_VAPID_SUBJECT . Strong approvals still follow the WebAuthn policy.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose common connection, catalog, policy, YAML, and runtime errors.
text: Start with the HTTP status or tool error and check the active profile. MCP returns HTTP 401 Check the profile bearer token, expiry, and revocation status. Use the MCP endpoint and a Streamable HTTP client. Missing tool or empty catalog Check the token’s profile, tool name and profile patterns. Refresh the client catalog after edits. Code Mode must be enabled explicitly. Denied by policy or broker_required Read the rule named in the tool result. A hard denial requires a policy change or a different permitted operation. Use the applicable broker for operations it owns. Approval did not start the operation Retry the exact operation after approval and before expiry. Keep your token, profile, arguments, and working directory the same. YAML save returns 409 or 422 For 409, reload the manifest and reconcile concurrent edits. For 422, fix the reported YAML or schema error. Application fails to start Check the configured HTTPS consent origin and RP ID, SQLite write permissions, and the Node.js version used to install native modules. Use a shared PostgreSQL database for multiple replicas. Code Mode timed out Reduce the number of calls and the result size. Check the call summary before retrying because a tool may already have completed. Report a problem Include the version, runtime, tool name, error, and a redacted configuration excerpt. Keep credentials and private payloads out of the report.
